root_cause_label: CUDA-enabled PyTorch installation via plain pip3 install torch exhausts step budget
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 6 the agent issued `pip3 install torch` without specifying the CPU-only index URL, triggering a 530MB CUDA-enabled download (plus gigabytes of NVIDIA CUDA libraries) that never completed within the remaining 11 steps, all of which were consumed by empty wait commands.
t_err_evidence: Step 6 terminal output shows `Downloading torch-2.11.0-cp313-cp313-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl (530.7 MB)` and collection of nvidia-cudnn-cu13, nvidia-cublas, nvidia-nccl-cu13, nvidia-nvshmem-cu13, triton and other large CUDA packages — the result of `pip3 install torch` without a CPU-only index URL.
t_commit_evidence: Once the full CUDA-enabled torch download (530MB torch wheel + hundreds of MB of CUDA libraries) is initiated in step 6, the download cannot complete within the remaining step budget; no recovery action is attempted thereafter.
t_surface_evidence: The terminal output at step 6 already shows the massive CUDA dependency chain being resolved and the 530.7 MB torch wheel beginning to download, clearly indicating the wrong (CUDA) variant was selected.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked awareness that `pip3 install torch` on a CPU-only server defaults to the CUDA-enabled build. The correct approach is to specify `--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`, which would install a much smaller CPU-only torch package. The agent had no indication in the task spec or environment to prompt this distinction, and did not know to look for it.
